To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transmission of vibration through four anti-vibration gloves was not greatly affected by the magnitude of vibration but highly dependent on the force applied to a handle and highly variable between subjects.
glove transmissibility is highly dependent on push-force and highly dependent on the subject’s hand, and that the variability between subjects is greater than the variability between gloves.
the vibration transmissibilities of four anti-vibration gloves were not greatly affected when the push force was changed, but the transmissibilities varied greatly between gloves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of gloves on the transmission of vibration through the hand and arm.
quantifying the extent to which a ‘good’ anti-vibration glove can reduce hand-arm vibration exposure in a range of typical work situations.
the transmission of hand-transmitted vibration through anti-vib gloves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ISO 10819 is inadequate for the evaluation of anti-vibration gloves.

the transmissibility of a glove is dependent on the force between the hand inside the glove and the handle of a tool and is also dependent on the hand inside the gloves, but not dependent on the vibration magnitude.

the transmission of vibration through the four anti-vibration gloves tested was highly dependent on push forces and that there is a need for a standardised test that includes a wide range of forces representative to those occurring in work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current ISO 10819 is not fit for purpose and should be revised to include a range of push forces and a range of hands.

the variability between subjects is greater than the variability between gloves and therefore that the standardised test of gloves should be performed on a wide range of subjects and with a range of push forces.
the variability in vibration transmission between hands is at least as great as the variation between gloves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a standard for anti-vib glove testing should include a wide force range and a wide range of subjects.
a test protocol for anti-vibration glove performance should be designed to include a wide range and number of hands, and a wide range of push forces.
the current standard is not adequate to reflect the performance of gloves in real use.
